# everpure_azure_storage_pool (Resource)

Manages a Storage Pool — a block storage instance injected into a virtual network in your subscription.

Creation is asynchronous and can take up to 90 minutes. A Reservation must already exist in the same subscription and region.

~> **Deleting a storage pool is permanent.** There is no soft delete. The API refuses to delete a pool that still holds volume groups, volumes or other resources, including soft-deleted ones awaiting eradication. See [Deletion policies](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure/latest/docs/guides/deletion-policies).

To read a storage pool managed elsewhere without taking ownership of it, use the [`everpure_azure_storage_pool` data source](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure/latest/docs/data-sources/azure_storage_pool).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    everpure = {
      source = "PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure"
    }
    azurerm = {
      source  = "hashicorp/azurerm"
      version = ">= 4.0"
    }
  }
}

# Credentials: `az login` by default, or the ARM_* environment variables /
# provider attributes described in the Authentication guide. The subscription
# can also be set via ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID.
provider "everpure" {
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

provider "azurerm" {
  features {}
  subscription_id = var.subscription_id
}

variable "subscription_id" {
  type = string
}

variable "reservation_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "Full ARM ID of an existing Everpure Reservation in the same subscription and region."
}

resource "azurerm_resource_group" "example" {
  name     = "rg-storage-prod"
  location = "eastus2"
}

resource "azurerm_virtual_network" "example" {
  name                = "vnet-prod"
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.example.name
  location            = azurerm_resource_group.example.location
  address_space       = ["10.0.0.0/16"]
}

# The pool is injected into a subnet delegated to the Everpure service.
resource "azurerm_subnet" "storage" {
  name                 = "snet-storage"
  resource_group_name  = azurerm_resource_group.example.name
  virtual_network_name = azurerm_virtual_network.example.name
  address_prefixes     = ["10.0.1.0/24"]

  delegation {
    name = "everpure"
    service_delegation {
      name = "PureStorage.Block/storagePools"
    }
  }
}

resource "everpure_azure_storage_pool" "example" {
  name                = "pool-prod-east"
  resource_group_name = azurerm_resource_group.example.name
  location            = azurerm_resource_group.example.location
  zone                = "1"
  reservation_id      = var.reservation_id

  # Megabytes per second. Can be changed in place.
  provisioned_bandwidth_in_mbps = 2048

  vnet_injection {
    subnet_id = azurerm_subnet.storage.id
  }

  # Enables platform console access (GUI, REST API and CLI) from the injected
  # subnet. Remove the block to disable console access.
  platform_console {
    gui_enabled = true
    api_enabled = true
    cli_enabled = false
  }

  tags = {
    environment = "prod"
  }

  # Pool deletion is permanent. This makes any plan that would destroy or
  # replace the pool fail. See the "Deletion policies" guide.
  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }

  # Optional: override the default per-operation timeouts. Creation defaults
  # to 95m already; this raises it further for a slower region or subscription.
  timeouts {
    create = "120m"
  }
}

output "storage_pool_id" {
  value = everpure_azure_storage_pool.example.id
}

output "storage_pool_provisioned_iops" {
  value = everpure_azure_storage_pool.example.provisioned_iops
}

output "storage_pool_console_management_ip" {
  value = everpure_azure_storage_pool.example.platform_console[0].subnet[0].management_ip_address
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `location` (String) Azure region the pool is created in, using the canonical short name, e.g. `eastus2`. Must match the region of the Reservation. Changing this forces a new pool to be created.
- `name` (String) Name of the storage pool. The name must be 1-127 characters long and contain only letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores. Changing this forces a new pool to be created.
- `provisioned_bandwidth_in_mbps` (Number) Bandwidth provisioned for the pool, in megabytes per second (MB/s). Must be at least 800. Can be changed in place, without replacing the pool.
- `reservation_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the Reservation that funds this pool, e.g. the `id` of an [`everpure_azure_reservation`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PureStorage-OpenConnect/everpure-azure/latest/docs/resources/azure_reservation) resource. The Reservation must already exist in the same subscription and region. Changing this forces a new pool to be created.
- `resource_group_name` (String) Name of the resource group the pool lives in. Changing this forces a new pool to be created.
- `zone` (String) Availability zone within the region, e.g. `"1"`. Set to `""` for a region with no availability zones. Changing this forces a new pool to be created, destroying all data on the existing pool.

### Optional

- `platform_console` (Block List) Platform console access (GUI, REST API and CLI) from the injected subnet. Remove this block to disable console access entirely; when present, at least one of `gui_enabled`, `api_enabled` or `cli_enabled` must be explicitly set to `true`. Can be changed in place. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--platform_console))
- `tags` (Map of String) A mapping of tags to assign to the pool. Can be changed in place. Some environments append their own tags outside Terraform (e.g. an Azure Policy); including those tags in this configuration, or excluding them via a `lifecycle.ignore_changes` block, avoids a persistent diff against them.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `vnet_injection` (Block List) The virtual network and subnet the pool is injected into. Exactly one injection is supported today. Changing this forces a new pool to be created. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--vnet_injection))

### Read-Only

- `data_retention_period_in_seconds` (Number) How long a destroyed volume group, volume or snapshot is kept before being eradicated, in seconds.
- `id` (String) The full Azure Resource Manager ID of the storage pool, e.g. `/subscriptions/.../resourceGroups/.../providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool1`.
- `internal_id` (String) Everpure's internal ID of the storage pool.
- `provisioned_iops` (Number) Total I/O operations per second (IOPS) provisioned for the pool. Derived from `provisioned_bandwidth_in_mbps`; shown as known only after apply whenever the pool is created or updated.

<a id="nestedblock--platform_console"></a>
### Nested Schema for `platform_console`

Optional:

- `api_enabled` (Boolean) Whether REST API access is enabled. Must equal `gui_enabled`. Defaults to `false` for the same reason as `gui_enabled`.
- `cli_enabled` (Boolean) Whether CLI (SSH) access is enabled. Defaults to `false` for the same reason as `gui_enabled` and `api_enabled`: at least one service must be enabled whenever `platform_console` is present, so leaving all three unset is rejected rather than silently enabling every service.
- `gui_enabled` (Boolean) Whether GUI access is enabled. Must equal `api_enabled`. Defaults to `false`, along with `api_enabled` and `cli_enabled`: an otherwise-empty `platform_console` block enables no service, and is rejected — at least one must be set to `true`.

Read-Only:

- `default_username` (String) Default username for console access, system-populated.
- `subnet` (Attributes List) Per-subnet console access details, system-populated. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--platform_console--subnet))
- `subnet_ids` (List of String) Subnets enabled for console access. Always the `vnet_injection` subnet.

<a id="nestedatt--platform_console--subnet"></a>
### Nested Schema for `platform_console.subnet`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the subnet.
- `management_ip_address` (String) Management IP address assigned to the subnet.
- `service_backend_ip_addresses` (List of String) Service backend IP addresses assigned to the subnet.



<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) Defaults to 95 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when creating the pool.
- `delete` (String) Defaults to 95 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when destroying the pool.
- `read` (String) Defaults to 5 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when reading the pool.
- `update` (String) Defaults to 30 minutes. A duration string: a number with a unit suffix s (seconds), m (minutes) or h (hours); segments can be combined, e.g. "30m" or "1h30m". Used when updating the pool.


<a id="nestedblock--vnet_injection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `vnet_injection`

Required:

- `subnet_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the delegated subnet the pool's network interfaces are placed in.

Read-Only:

- `virtual_network_id` (String) Full Azure Resource Manager ID of the virtual network `subnet_id` belongs to. Derived from `subnet_id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = everpure_azure_storage_pool.example
  identity = {
    subscription_id     = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
    resource_group_name = "rg-storage-prod"
    name                = "pool-prod-east"
  }
}

resource "everpure_azure_storage_pool" "example" {
  # ... configuration matching the imported storage pool
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the storage pool.
- `resource_group_name` (String) Name of the resource group the resource lives in.
- `subscription_id` (String) Azure subscription ID the resource lives in.

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Storage pools are imported by their full Azure resource ID.
terraform import everpure_azure_storage_pool.example \
  "/subscriptions/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/resourceGroups/rg-storage-prod/providers/PureStorage.Block/storagePools/pool-prod-east"
```
